He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]], and was drafted 20th overall in the [[2017 NBA draft]] by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. He has also played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Sacramento Kings]], [[Brooklyn Nets]], and [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. ==High school career== ===Freshman and sophomore seasons=== Giles attended [[Wesleyan Christian Academy]] in [[High Point, North Carolina]], where he was coached by [[Keith Gatlin]]. As a freshman, Giles averaged 12.5 [[points per game]] and 9.5 [[rebounds per game]] after leading Wesleyan Christian to a 2013 NCISAA 3A State Championship alongside future and former NBA player [[Theo Pinson]].{{cite web|url= https://www.tarheeltimes.com/article46462.aspx|title=Harry Giles, Theo Pinson lead Wesleyan to State Title|date=February 24, 2013|website=Tar Heel Times|access-date=August 8, 2023}} Giles missed his entire sophomore year due to a left knee injury.{{Cite news|url=http://www.greensboro.com/harry-giles-will-miss-sophomore-season-after-knee-surgery/article_749ec98e-f4ac-11e2-bf29-0019bb30f31a.html|title=Harry Giles will miss sophomore season after knee surgery|last=Reynolds|first=David|date=July 24, 2013|work=greensboro.com|access-date=April 16, 2017}} During the 2014 summer, Giles would return from injury joining Team CP3 on the EYBL circuit.{{cite |website=cbssports.com}} ==Professional career== ===Sacramento Kings (2017–2020)=== On June 22, 2017, Giles was selected by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] with the 20th overall pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]]. His rights were later traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] on draft night. Giles would sit out the entire [[2017 NBA Summer League]]. On July 8, 2017, Giles signed his rookie contract with the Kings worth $10.6 million over 4 years.{{Cite web|title=Harry Giles Salary & Contract {{!}} Salary Sport|url=https://salarysport.com/basketball/player/harry-giles/|access-date=2020-08-15|website=salarysport.com}}{{Cite news|url= https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-fox-jackson-giles/|title=King's sign Fox, Jackson, and Giles|work=nba.com|access-date=July 9, 2017}} On October 6, 2017, it was announced Giles would make his NBA debut in January 2018. On January 18, 2018, it was announced that Giles would sit out the rest of the season.{{Cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/harry-giles-update-011818|title=Harry Giles Update {{!}} Sacramento Kings|work=Sacramento Kings|access-date=January 18, 2018}} On May 14, 2018, ''[[The Sacramento Bee]]'' announced that Giles would participate in the California Classic Summer League on July 2, 3, and 5 in Sacramento.{{Cite news|url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/nba/sacramento-kings/kings-blog/article211097519.html|title=Dates set for 3 days of summer-league games in Sacramento. Here's what to expect|access-date=May 27, 2018}} Giles joined the Kings for the [[2018 NBA Summer League]]. In his NBA debut on October 17, 2018, Giles scored 2 points in a 123–117 season-opening loss against the [[Utah Jazz]]. On November 10, 2018, Giles was assigned to the [[Stockton Kings]], the G League affiliate of the Kings, where he scored 30 points in his debut for the team. On November 11, 2018, Giles was recalled by the Kings. On January 31, 2019, Giles recorded a career-high 20 points and 7 rebounds in a 135–113 victory over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071435|title=Giles, Bagley lead Kings in 135–113 blowout of Hawks|work=[[ESPN]]|access-date=March 8, 2023}} On April 3, the Kings shut down Giles for the remainder of the season.{{Cite news|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/kings-shut-down-rookie-harry-000840306.html|title=Kings shut down rookie Harry Giles for remainder of NBA Season|work=yahoo.com|access-date=April 3, 2019|archive-date=April 6, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190406152758/https://sports.yahoo.com/kings-shut-down-rookie-harry-000840306.html|url-status=dead}} On October 31, 2019, the Kings declined Giles's option for the 2020–21 season worth $4 million.
